commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix composition conditioned the Brazil IEEPA carve-out on the witness exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` rather than on Section 232 aluminum membership, so it charged the 40% Brazil surcharge on aluminum articles that headings 9903.01.83 / 9903.85.02 except from heading 9903.01.77.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 96 (read the diff in full): Brazil gate re-grounded in `ieepa_component_rate` (post line 2367) and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (post line 2523); steel provenance re-cited on `ch99c_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate`, rate '0.50' and formula unchanged. Like ch99a this file uses `from:` rather than `effective_from:` for version windows. Chunk covered all four expected indices 96-99; the bundle has the full 100 module files and every one of the 100 diffs carries this same two-part change, so dedup before benchmarking.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical (the steel half of the diff is pure provenance: `ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate` keeps `formula: '0.50'` and only its `source:` string and two proof-atom citation paths move from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02), but the other two hunks change executable meaning in two rules' version formulas, so the module change is not provenance-only. The pre-fix chapter-wide composition gated the Brazil IEEPA surcharge carve-out on `entry_is_line_b`, which the same file uses as the caller-supplied exemplar flag standing in for the witness's single aluminum line (line 1925: `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` ... `formula: entry_is_line_b`); "line b" appears nowhere in the HTS, so the branch condition had no source basis while the rule's own unchanged proof atom claims the statutory exception ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02"). I verified the carve-out is class-based, not line-based, through the pinned release: 9903.01.77 imposes +40% on Brazil "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90", and 9903.01.83 covers "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum" — so re-grounding the gate on `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` is exactly the untraceable-branch repair, not new coverage or a scope enhancement.

triage.verifier_notes:
inferred from verified sibling module index 96 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Kind check against alternatives: not polarity_or_logic (the `not` is unchanged; only the operand moved), not unrepresented_clause (the exception branch already existed pre-fix, wrongly predicated), not amount_mismatch (0.50 and brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate untouched), not wrong_period_or_effective_date (all effective_from unchanged). The runner-up is wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out reached the wrong population), but the decisive fact is that the predicate itself — a witness-fixture identifier — has no counterpart in the cited source and was re-grounded, which is the definition given for untraceable_branch.

Two cautions for the reviewer. (1) The first reader's quote is PR-level and mostly describes work not in this commit's ch98 diff: the "Section 232 steel component the witness never had" already exists in the parent (a9562cfd) — here it changes only by citation string — and adding it would in any case be new coverage, not a defect. The decisive evidence is the diff line, not that PR-body sentence. (2) The repair is partial: `entry_is_line_b` survives in the post file at line 1925 as the formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`, and 9903.01.83 also excludes iron/steel, copper, vehicles, semiconductors and wood products from the Brazil 40%, none of which the post-fix gate covers. That is residual under-coverage, not a reason to doubt that the pre-fix state was wrong.

Provenance note: resolving the cited atom's locator `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219` against the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, corpus commit e79781bd) returns a Rev. 3 page of bare subheading numbers, not the quoted exclusion sentence — the same stale-locator-for-this-vintage pattern the commit report flags for 9903.81.x. The substantive exclusion is nonetheless verified directly at 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83.
